segments.text: Yatyaidam sarva-siddhreshesya-shedirthaya shriyantasisya-dhreshetaya-next-sudra.
A kuruva-prakashana-mukhtam naita-dhurgatam.
What has already been explained that for such a yogi this whole objective world is
his own self.
He perceives this whole objective world as one with his own self.
And his personal body, he feels just like an object.
It is already explained.
This kind of achievement is not difficult for such a yogi.
Because friday-yatya-sangat-tarth-dresh-sop-darshanam, when the thoughts of one's mind are
diverged to the heart, the center of God consciousness.
When all the thoughts of one's mind are diverted to the heart, heart means the center of God
consciousness.
They are diverted, sentence to that, then dresh-sop-darshanam, then one feels the existence of God
consciousness in objective world and the world of negation in oneness.
He feels the existence of objective world and the existence of negation of it.
Do you know when negation of this objective world comes at the time of death, at the time
of sociality, sound sleep, the negation comes of objective world.
In that also, he feels the existence of God consciousness in an easy way.
Vishya pratishtha-sthana-tath-chit-prakasho-radha-yam, the heart means, does not mean the heart which
is already situated in our own body.
Not that heart, it is chit-prakasha.
Heart means here, chit-prakasha, the light of consciousness, the light of consciousness,
which is the background of the whole universe, background of the existence of whole universe.
The light of consciousness is the background, basis.
On that basis, this whole universe is moving here and there and dying, getting birth,
crying, enjoying, smiling, loving, marrying, everything comes out of that.
But in that basis, on that basis, there, the yogi, what he does, tathra-chit-sanga-tath,
he collects his mind there and puts that in that, on that point, how chalata-chalata-tade-kagra-bhavanath,
although the mind is always flickering, it does not exist in one point.
But by the bhavanai, by the sadhana of one point in this, it becomes easy.
Then kneel-deh-prana-bhuddha-atmanai, drasya means the object world, that is already all
external objects, object world does not mean external objects only.
The world means external objects, at the same time, your body of wakefulness, body of
dreaming state, body of dreamless state and body of wireless, too.
That is also included in object world.
So this whole universe is object world, including body, bodies.
This is what he explains, how he explains drasya, drasya means kneel-deh-prana-bhuddha-atmanai.
And then saapasya, saapudarshanam, saapa means aetat-abhavru paasya.
The negation of these also, the negation means that wiredness, that is shunya.
And he perceives that, perceives in which way, takt-grah-grah-gavibhadeena, yathavastu, saunga-kalpada-ya-prakashanam-bhavati.
This is differentiatedness of objectivity and subjectivity.
He discards away, he keeps away, he gets away from this differentiation of object and subject.
Objective consciousness, perception and subjective perceptions are removed by him.
And in its real way, yathavastu, in its real way, saunga-kalpada-ya-prakashanam-bhavati,
he feels this whole universe as his own limbs of his universal body.
Chit prakashatam abhene vishmanam hi chitam, when you make your mind enter in the light of consciousness,
when you make your mind enter in the light of consciousness, then your mind feels this whole universe as one with that universal being.
The one who has sentenced all his organs, including mind, in the voidness of that chit prakashat, heart.
Riddhya kase, heart, heart does not mean this heart of flesh.
It may stop someday and will die.
That heart is not explained here. The real heart, yes, light of consciousness is heart.
The one who puts all his organs one pointedly on that heart of light of consciousness,
Padmasam Putamaddhaga, and remains in between two lotuses of this and I.
Thisness is one lotus, and Iness is another lotus, between these two of thisness and Iness.
He is situated, he is situated, his consciousness, between these two worlds, two lotuses of this and I.
Anani chaita, when being one pointed there, Subhages, O Parvati, Param Savavagya Mahavanya,
he becomes glorified with God consciousness.
Param Yadra Savavagya, the glory here in this shloka means vishayasaratapati.
He becomes the king of the whole universe, the ruler of the whole universe.
Tattvṛti samāpannam mahāyoginam uddhiśya shrīma-sacchandepī.
In sacchandra tantra also, for such a yogi, nominating such a yogi, he has explained,
sacchandra tantra has explained, that such a sarvēshu-bhūtēshu, bāvta tēndrēshu-chāvaram-jangamam-chāyva-chētana-chētana-msitam,
adanam-viyāpis-sarvam-tu-sama-resin-sam-sitam.
Sacayogi, parvēts, this whole universe, adanam.
Adanam means this whole universe is, viyāpia-parvēded by sacayogi.
Sarvam means whole, and he becomes sama-resin-sam-sitam.
He is situated as one with that whole universe.
So his consciousness is called, not god consciousness, then his god consciousness will be transformed
in the name of universal consciousness, sarvēshu-bhūtēshu, because he parvēts these whole classes
of beings in moods, in elements, in organic world, in the re-esitāya, in innate and
unenate objects, whatever is existing in this world, he parvēts everything and thus becomes
one with that universal consciousness.
And spandā it is concluded in this shloka tādhā sāthman nidhiśtāna sarvēth-travam-bhāvisiti.
You have not to reside.
Don't try to reside in each and every being.
Residing in one's own self.
When you reside in one's own self, you'll reside in this whole universe, too.
Because your real self is one with universe.
As you reside and you are established in the existence of self, you'll be established
already in you, in your self-self.
